statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44173: MariaDB Server ran SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE and SELECT ... INTO DUMPFILE without checking the FILE privilege when the FROM clause contained only subqueries, so an account without FILE could write files wherever the server is allowed to write, within the limits of --secure-file-priv and filesystem permissions (GHSA-667j-m53j-wpmc, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-667j-m53j-wpmc, MDEV-39493). MariaDB fixed it in 11.4.11 and 11.8.7, released on 18 May 2026, with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/c0fb8448332972fce3adc176f195a573f9fdc83d, which makes mysql_execute_command() in sql/sql_parse.cc and mysql_test_select() in sql/sql_prepare.cc check the global FILE privilege before the per-table SELECT check. Alpine records the fix at mariadb 11.4.11-r0 in its 3.23 security database (https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json). We checked every mariadb build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository as of 2026-11-28, 11.4.9-r0, 11.4.10-r0, 11.4.11-r0, 11.4.12-r0, 11.4.13-r0 and 11.4.14-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64: the embedded server library libmariadbd.so.19 in each build's mariadb-embedded package and /usr/bin/mariadb-backup in its mariadb-backup package carry the MariaDB server version string that matches its package version (11.4.9-MariaDB to 11.4.14-MariaDB). The fix adds no distinctive string, so the boundary rests on those upstream release versions: 11.4.11-r0 is the first build on a MariaDB release that includes the fix, so the range ends there and the earlier builds are affected.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44173: MariaDB Server ran SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE and SELECT ... INTO DUMPFILE without checking the FILE privilege when the FROM clause contained only subqueries, so an account without FILE could write files wherever the server is allowed to write, within the limits of --secure-file-priv and filesystem permissions (GHSA-667j-m53j-wpmc, https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-667j-m53j-wpmc, MDEV-39493). MariaDB fixed it in 11.4.11 and 11.8.7, released on 18 May 2026, with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/c0fb8448332972fce3adc176f195a573f9fdc83d, which makes mysql_execute_command() in sql/sql_parse.cc and mysql_test_select() in sql/sql_prepare.cc check the global FILE privilege before the per-table SELECT check. Debian fixes it in trixie with mariadb 1:11.8.8-0+deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-44173). Every mariadb build published in the DHI Debian repository as of 2026-11-28 is one of four DHI rebuilds of Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1, each with 56 binary packages per architecture including the -dbgsym packages, on amd64 and arm64. That Debian version is MariaDB 11.8.6, which predates the fix (/usr/bin/mariadb-backup in all four builds on both architectures reports 11.8.6-MariaDB), and the Debian changelog shipped in each of the four builds on both architectures does not mention this CVE or MDEV-39493. Every published build is therefore affected until the owner ships MariaDB 11.8.7 or later, or a backport of the fix.
